close_reason: Consolidated fix with PKIX-7f92.39 (same parameter, both bounds). Added private MAX_OCTETS_RANGE = 1..=21 and shared validate_max_octets helper. set_parameter and with_max_octets both route through the validator: set_parameter returns ParameterError::InvalidValue; with_max_octets panics (precedent: LintRunner::new's panic-on-duplicate-id). Range is 1..=21 to accommodate both RFC readings the workspace documents (encoded-content=20, unsigned-value=21); anything outside is rejected. Five regression tests cover both paths and both directions. 300 tests pass; workspace builds clean.
description:
rfc5280.rs:148-170: set_parameter('max-octets', '...') rejects 0 but accepts any other usize, including 21, 1000, usize::MAX. The rustdoc says 'Setting max-octets above 20 is permitted but advertises a deliberate deviation from RFC 5280 baseline' — but there is no surfaced signal (no log, no Notice finding, no separate metadata field) that distinguishes a deviation from a baseline run.

Failure mode: an operator copy-pastes an OSCAL Profile that sets max-octets=64 (or worse, max-octets=usize::MAX as a 'temporary' workaround) and ships a runner that silently passes every cert under the RFC 5280 §4.1.2.2 check. The finding output is indistinguishable from a clean baseline run. Months later someone re-reads the Profile and discovers the regression.

Maintainer consequence: this is the kind of silent-misconfig bug that produces 'pkix-lint said clean, why was the cert noncompliant' tickets. Two cheap fixes: (a) emit a Notice-severity finding tied to the same lint ID when max_octets > 20 (operator sees the deviation in normal output); (b) reject set_parameter values > 20 with InvalidValue, forcing operators to wire a separate explicit 'permit-rfc-deviation' lint when they really want this. (b) is the safer default for a Tier-1 RFC-conformance lint.
title: Rfc5280MaxSerialLengthLint set_parameter accepts values >20 silently weakening RFC baseline
